cards.text: Jeremiah, a prophet, is carrying the word of the LORD to His people, Israel, and the LORD is NOT here for small talk. Long ago, He says, they broke their yoke and tore off their chains.

cards.question: Israel breaks the yoke and tears off the chains. What are they saying as they do it?

cards.text: Then comes a hard picture: on every high hill and under every green tree, Israel lay down as a prostitute. And the LORD reminds them He had planted them like a choice vine from the very best seed.

cards.question: The LORD planted Israel like a choice vine. What does He say they turned themselves into?
Israel can wash with lye and plenty of soap, but the ___ of their guilt is still before the LORD.

cards.text: Friend, that's me with a burnt cookie sheet: I scrub for an HOUR, hold it up to the light, and the stain's STILL sitting there smiling at me. Then the LORD repeats what Israel says about the Baals.

cards.question: Israel admits they have run after the Baals.

cards.text: Look at your behavior in the valley, the LORD says. Israel is a swift young she-camel galloping here and there, a wild donkey sniffing the wind in the heat of her desire.

cards.question: In the LORD's picture, anyone looking for that wild donkey has to wear themselves out to find her.

cards.text: The LORD says they should have kept their feet from going bare and their throats from being thirsty. All that galloping here and there? That's me when every oven timer in the bakery goes off at ONCE.

cards.question: Israel could stop chasing. So why do they say it's hopeless?

cards.text: As a thief is ashamed when he's caught, so Israel is disgraced, kings, officials, priests and prophets included. I know that caught face, friend. I make it every time a baker walks in on me with a mustache full of cookie dough.

cards.question: The house of Israel, kings and priests and prophets included, says to a ___, 'You are my father,' and to a ___, 'You gave me birth.'

cards.text: They've turned their backs to the LORD and not their faces. Yet in the time of trouble, they say, 'Rise up and save us!'

cards.question: Trouble hits, and Israel cries, 'Rise up and save us!' What does the LORD say back?

answers.text: Let the gods they made save them
He is already on His way to them
They should wait for Him at the temple

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out to Judah, the kingdom of His people in the south: your gods are as numerous as your cities. A god in EVERY town, friend, and not one of them answering the phone.

cards.question: When Israel brings a case against Him, the LORD says only a few of them have rebelled.

cards.text: The LORD says He struck their sons, but it was in vain. They accepted no discipline.

cards.question: A sword devoured Israel's prophets like a voracious lion. Whose sword was it?

cards.text: Now this generation is told to consider the word of the LORD. And the LORD asks: Has He been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of dense darkness?

cards.question: God's people say they are free to roam and will come to Him no more.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks: Does a maiden forget her jewelry, or a bride her wedding sash? Friend, I've walked out of this bakery without my apron, but NOBODY walks into her own wedding without that sash.

cards.question: A bride never forgets her wedding sash. How long have God's people forgotten Him?

cards.text: The LORD says they pursue love so skillfully, even the most immoral of women could learn from their ways.

cards.question: The LORD says Israel's skirts are stained with blood. Whose blood is it?
In spite of all these things, Israel says they are innocent.

cards.text: They even say, 'Surely His anger will turn from me.' That's me holding an empty cookie box with crumbs all down my apron going, 'What cookies?'

cards.question: The LORD says He will judge them because they say, 'I have not ___.'

cards.text: The LORD says, 'How impulsive you are, constantly changing your ways!' That's me at the topping station: sprinkles, no, chocolate chips, no, WAIT, sprinkles.

cards.question: Israel will be disappointed by Egypt, just as they were by ___.

cards.text: The LORD has rejected those they trust. They will not prosper by their help.

cards.question: After Egypt lets them down, how does the LORD say Israel will leave?

answers.text: With their hands on their heads
With their arms full of gold
With a new army behind them

cards.text: Then the LORD asks: If a man divorces his wife and she marries another, can he ever return to her? Wouldn't such a land be completely defiled?

cards.question: Israel has played the harlot with many lovers. What does the LORD ask them?

answers.text: Whether they would return to Him
Whether Egypt will take them in

cards.text: Lift up your eyes to the barren heights, the LORD says. They sat beside the highways waiting for their lovers, like a nomad in the desert, and they defiled the land.

cards.question: Because Israel defiled the land, the showers have been withheld, and no spring ___ have fallen.

cards.text: Yet they have the brazen look of a prostitute and refuse to be ashamed. And they've just called to the LORD, 'My Father, You are my friend from youth.'
Then they ask, 'Will He be angry forever? Will He be indignant to the end?'

cards.question: After asking whether the LORD will be angry forever, Israel stops doing evil.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "The LORD says they should have kept...", "All that galloping here and there?" and "That's me when every oven timer...".

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card's joke uses the galloping from Jeremiah 2:23, but the card cites only Jeremiah 2:25. Card 6 widened its citation to 2:22-23 for its stain callback. This card should cite Jeremiah 2:23-25 the same way.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "As a thief is ashamed...", "I know that caught face, friend." and "I make it every time...".

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The two-blank card makes the baker guess which word goes with which line: tree with 'You are my father' and stone with 'You gave me birth'. No earlier card sets up idols of wood and stone. The baker can't reason out that order, so it is guessing wording they haven't seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "no spring ___ have fallen" right after "the showers have been withheld" gives the answer away. 'Crops' and 'flowers' don't fall and aren't the same kind of thing as rains, so 'rains' is the only answer that fits.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Story cards 12, 14, 16, 18 and 19 are plain retellings with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice, reactions or humor. The second half of the stop reads like a summary.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card introduces Judah as "the kingdom of His people in the south." That fact comes from outside the passage (1 Kings 12), but the card cites only Jeremiah 2:28. Stop 1 card 1 does the same with "Jeremiah, a prophet." The docs say outside facts carry their reference, and also that a card cites exactly the verses it tells, no wider. The single "verses" field can't hold both.
findings.question: When a story card states an outside fact to introduce a new person or place, should its reference go in the card's "verses" field, in the card text, or nowhere?
